decision.case_state: Check-out works (carpet replacement and repaint) at Flat 21, 11 Juniper Mews. A quote totalling £605 (£220 paint, £240 carpet, £100 bathroom vinyl, £45 sink waste; VAT status not stated) was sent to the landlord on 2024-10-09 (event 013) asking for a go-ahead. No written landlord reply is on file. The ticket is on hold, waiting for the landlord, review 2024-10-11.

next_actions.action: Tell the provider not to order carpet or parts, and ask which company is quoting (Cedar Utilities on file or Sawyer on the quote), until written landlord approval is received.
Ask the landlord for a written yes or no on the £605 quote, since the provider's claim of a phone approval is not a landlord decision.
Hold the ticket for the landlord's reply, review on 2024-10-11.

boundaries: The provider's email (event 015) that the landlord said go ahead is hearsay and is not recorded as approval.
Sending the messages does not mean the landlord has approved the quote, and no contractor has been assigned or instructed.
No visit date exists in the record; the tenant has not been contacted about the visit.
Sending the quote figures does not confirm they are final or include VAT.
remaining_work: Landlord to give a written yes or no on the £605 quote (owner: landlord; review 2024-10-11).
Provider to confirm the company name and to book the visit once approved (owner: provider).
Resolve the landlord name conflict (Oscar in event 013, Ruben in event 014) before any approval is recorded.
Once approved, assign the contractor and set up the visit with the tenant, then record the result, invoice and close.
missing_info: Written landlord approval of the quote; no landlord reply is on file.
Landlord's name (Oscar or Ruben) and contact details; the property record has none.
Which company is quoting (Cedar Utilities or Sawyer).
Whether the £605 figures include VAT (the quote does not say).
Visit date and tenant contact outcome; no visit is booked in the record.
decision.summary: The provider says the landlord approved by phone and will order parts tomorrow, but no landlord decision is on file and the landlord's written reply to the 2024-10-09 quote request is outstanding. I told the provider not to order yet and asked which company is quoting, asked the landlord for a written yes or no, and put the job on hold until 2024-10-11.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: The quote (£605 across four items) went to the landlord on 2024-10-09 for approval. No written decision is on file. The provider's email says the landlord approved by phone, which is hearsay and not recorded. No visit is booked and the tenant has not been contacted about the visit. Outstanding: landlord's written approval, landlord name conflict, provider company conflict, VAT status, and the visit.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: (1) Email the provider (Sawyer / Cedar Utilities) to hold off ordering and to confirm the quoting company (ledger A1). (2) Email the landlord for a written yes or no on the £605 quote (ledger A2). The job is on hold with a review on 2024-10-11 (ledger A5).

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Not yet. The landlord decision is theirs and they have not replied; the wait is within the 3-day window, so chasing is premature. Escalate if the landlord is silent after the 2024-10-11 review, or if the provider's phone-approval claim turns out to conflict with the landlord's reply.

actions_claimed.description: Email to Sawyer (Cedar Utilities): do not order parts until written landlord approval; confirm quoting company.
Email to landlord asking for written yes/no on the £605 quote.
Internal note recording the landlord name, provider company and property record conflicts.
Ticket on hold for landlord response, review 2024-10-11.

failed_actions.handling: put_on_hold was called with the wrong ticket reference (006-provider-says-landlord-approved). Found the real ref NBL-006-provider-says-landlord-approved via list_tickets and re-applied the hold, verified as A5.

conflicts: Event 015 (provider) says the landlord approved by phone; no landlord record of approval exists. Trusted the absence of a landlord decision and asked the landlord in writing.
Event 013 addresses the landlord as 'Oscar'; event 014 says 'Ruben'.
Event 013 quote is from 'Sawyer'; the assigned provider is Cedar Utilities (events 003 and 005).
Event 012 refers to a 'studio'; the property is Flat 21 (a flat).
assumptions: The landlord is the same person in events 013 and 014, and 'Oscar' and 'Ruben' are a name conflict, not two landlords.
The £605 total is the sum of the four quoted lines.

args.body:
Hi Sawyer,

Thanks for your message. We have not yet received written approval from the landlord for the quote, so please do not order the carpet or any parts yet. We are confirming the approval with the landlord directly and will let you know as soon as we have their decision.

Could you also confirm which company is quoting for this job? Our job was sent to Cedar Utilities, but the quote came from Sawyer.

Thanks,
Northbridge Lettings
